---
title: "Swiss Stats Explorer"
description: "Build a query from the codelists of a dataset and download the data."
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

The [Swiss Stats Explorer](https://stats.swiss/) (SSE) is the new data
platform of the BFS, based on the SDMX standard. It replaces STAT-TAB and
its PXWeb API (see
[Get started](introduction.html#from-stat-tab-to-the-swiss-stats-explorer)).

Each dataset has dimensions
(e.g. the commune, the year, the number of rooms), and each dimension has a
codelist: the codes of its values. You download data in two steps:

1. get the codelists with `bfs_get_sse_metadata()`,
2. select the codes you need and pass them to `bfs_get_sse_data()`.

```{r}
library(BFS)
library(dplyr)
```

## Find the dataset id

The dataset id (e.g. `DF_LWZ_1`, the vacant dwellings) is in the URL of the
dataset on [stats.swiss](https://stats.swiss/), after `df[id]=`.

## Get the codelists

```{r}
codelist <- bfs_get_sse_metadata("DF_LWZ_1", language = "en")
codelist
```

There is one row per value of each dimension:

- `code` and `text`: the dimension code and its label,
- `value` and `valueText`: the value code and its label.

List the dimensions with:

```{r}
distinct(codelist, code, text)
```

## Build the query

The query is a named list: the dimension codes as names, the value codes as
values. Filter the codelist on the labels you want:

```{r}
selection <- codelist |>
  filter(
    (code == "GR_KT_GDE" & valueText %in% c("Aarau", "Olten")) |
      (code == "WOHN_ANZAHL" & valueText == "Total") |
      (code == "LEERWOHN_TYP" & valueText == "Vacant dwelling for rent") |
      (code == "MEASURE_DIMENSION" & valueText == "Observed Value")
  )

query <- split(selection$value, selection$code)
query
```

A dimension not in the query keeps all its values.

## Download the data

```{r}
bfs_get_sse_data(
  number_bfs = "DF_LWZ_1",
  language = "en",
  query = query,
  start_period = "2020",
  end_period = "2023"
)
```

Use `column_name_type = "text"` for the dimension labels as column names,
`variable_value_type = "code"` for the codes instead of the labels, and
`clean_names = TRUE` for snake_case column names.

::: {.callout .callout-warning}
Without `query`, `bfs_get_sse_data()` downloads the whole dataset, which can
be large and slow.
:::
